73E3AF769BA04C62B14AD8DC615AABDE.description: 5.5 examine the traditions of the Black church as an instrument for political, social, and educational leadership

E867B9FAE9EA4FBF92C35B2E6575937A.description: 5.4 investigate how legal documents relate to the Canadian context regarding Confederation, Constitution. (e.g., UN documents, Charter of Rights and Freedom, Constitutional documents)

531AEFEA4BB94098AB91AE696EECDA96.description: 5.3 analyze the impact of the Civil-Rights Movement on people of African descent in Canada, and in particular, in Nova Scotia

1C9C996B30264A7A866901860E90D20C.description: 5.2 compare and contrast the history of the Civil-Rights Movement in Africa, United States, and Canada

B1A46EA3F1644B078E95636749330129.description:
5.1 examine the concept of power and the correlation between power, disenfranchisement,
segregation, and racism as these relate to the social conditions of people of African descent
(e.g., employment, housing, education, and politics)

80CB1B55349B4CD1837ADBE0A7B876CF.description: analyze critically the struggle of peoples of African descent for the pursuit of civil rights and equality

C75B1AC444DF4C048865EE65BDDB7857.description: 4.8 explain relationships and connections in the data studied (e.g., chronological ties, cause and effect, similarities and differences)

81EB3B702CD04631BAA006566DE6E8CD.description: 4.7 compare key interpretations of African Canadian studies

86BCC3B6E5D444C5BAE53BB4BE1A8A82.description: 4.6 demonstrate an ability to identify bias, prejudice, stereotyping, or a lack of substantiation in statements, arguments, and opinions

66F31232EF6A43A18A225968922D36F0.description: 4.5 organize research findings, using a variety of methods and forms: graphs, charts, maps, diagrams, etc.

51A13DB5971547B5B3D7A19B92F03E0A.description: 4.4 conduct an organized research, using a variety of information sources (e.g., audio-visual materials, internet sites) that present a diverse range of perspectives on African Canadian Studies

DA49668FB78E40C78D8DB1069CB5A4C2.description: 4.2 develop a work plan that enables time management, monitors progress, and contributes to the criteria for evaluation

26FD273B68CE4EC387F020DB66952590.description: 4.1 develop and refine a proposal for an inquiry or creative work

F777AC47EE21459D9DF9AC75F8AE897B.description: demonstrate effective skills in conducting research using historical methods and in communicating the results of their research effectively

BFCE58B64B814B3BA8D943AA770758AD.description: 3B.7 compare and contrast Black communities across Canada within changing demographics (e.g., Migration patterns, Immigration policy, expansion of Black communities after 1867)

EDC0E8D401BC4C2482F132C4BA954772.description: 3B.6 examine the implications of Confederation on Canada as a nation, and demonstrate an understanding of the contributions and roles that African Canadians have played in pre- and postconfederation (e.g., leadership in communities and society, military)

1F78B4289A6E42CA991165921D435ED3.description: 3B.5 identify the problems Black settlers experienced coming to Canada, (e.g., Slave Code Laws, legislation, environment, and settlement patterns)

48CA97A9AE7C436BB384C3E91C70AB6A.description: 3B.4 analyze the implications of the Civil War and its aftermath (the Emancipation Act and Reconstruction) on people of African descent

8BB09B30FD5B4E599D760FDC464CED9E.description: 3B.3 evaluate the impact of the Underground Railroad on the diaspora of African people within the United States and Canada

FE692E67C4EC4BA198A5D3300E9286BA.description: 3B.2 investigate why the Black Loyalists, Maroons, and Black Refugees immigrated to Canada

B75115DE717D43528DC5648AD1A4A010.description:
3B.1 examine the causes and outcomes of the American Revolution and its implications for people of
African descent

15A9082AFF9F42078B5850E1836EAE27.description:
demonstrate an understanding of the conditions of enslavement, strategies of resistance, and the
implications of enslavement on African Canadian settlement

42D7854BAC2A4ADC97139F559FBAFB36.description: 3A.6 examine how people of African descent used various means to resist enslavement through cultural expression (music, slave insurrections, religion, folktales, literature) and anti-slavery movements

C72FD7FBBBBB41E7AF8B528B67E87B42.description: 3A.5 explore the development (economical, political, social, spiritual) of slave culture in North America and the Caribbean and analyze the effects of enslavement on people of African descent

2B6E1DFC7CA849AC8599028747F309BB.description: 3A.3 compare and contrast the difference between displacement, migration, and force migration as these relate to the African people throughout the diaspora

835C342657B6480F9E6DABAE8A66EE22.description: 3A.2 examine the Transatlantic Slave Trade (routes, conditions, economics, etc.)

F321892F731649F6B66418486AEC1B3E.description: 3A.1 identify the colonial and imperial systems causing slavery

06C1BF0A658C49019AB246DF93E397BC.description: demonstrate an understanding of the impact of colonial expansion on the African diaspora

ED0D3CDA4256499E8536764FF9A79E00.description: 2.4 analyze the effects of these cultural components on the history of pre-colonial Africa and on the changes that took place from pre-colonial Africa to colonial Africa

CA09727BF8A044579EAB8F26E617CDC8.description: Describe a given 3-D object using words such as big, little, round, like a box, or like a can.

B201B4874F234B9996242D3F986CD70E.description: Create a representation of a given 3-D object using building blocks and compare the representation to the original 3-D object.

446DAA145DD44D21B5C6BD2C2A51D2A1.description: Students will be expected to build and describe 3-D objects. [CN, PS, V]

D999EB3B2A294723B10F8C07AF139FF9.description: Explain the sorting rule used to sort a pre-sorted set.

A21BE0EB0A414BCC9BD763CB7DBF989F.description: Sort a given set of familiar 3-D objects using one attribute, such as size or shape, and explain the sorting rule.

0756AAC3D4A94B009E4B9FB04F3004C6.description: Students will be expected to sort 3-D objects using one attribute. [C, CN, PS, R, V]

6FEA35CD84784629B764252467366FE5.description: Compare the volume of two given objects and explain the comparison using words such as bigger, smaller, or almost the same.

C9E3608FDD1F46979E2FCC191527DB8D.description: Compare the capacity of two given objects and explain the comparison using words such as holds less, holds more, or holds almost the same.

A48E7C5A56B0496EB247252AFB6E149E.description: Compare the mass of two given objects and explain the comparison using words such as lighter, heavier, or almost the same.

0956238BCD1F4ECA9D5E614BA904AD0F.description: Compare the length of two given objects and explain the comparison using words such as shorter, longer, taller, or almost the same.

09E339B9FE884E2F89E8DF697C47BA1A.description:
Students will be expected to use direct comparison to compare two objects based on a single
attribute, such as length, mass, volume, and capacity. [C, CN, PS, R, V]

1E744D705F774479BF91A7924778E04C.description: Identify and describe a repeating pattern containing two or three elements in its core in the classroom, the school, and outdoors.

AA35CD9443DD48C5AA6838A71273125C.description: Create a repeating pattern using manipulatives, musical instruments, or actions, and describe the pattern.

F64958BBA3B14DDA859498F403336BF8.description: Extend a variety of given repeating patterns to two more repetitions.

1447EE6927A645DBA7AAEA143C3B90C3.description: Reproduce a given repeating pattern and describe the pattern.

011B80639D5A451DA0276BA654327977.description: Distinguish between repeating patterns and non-repeating sequences in a given set by identifying the part that repeats.

0E155C201B85455CB603212E5837D2E5.description:
Students will be expected to demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns (two or three
elements) by identifying, describing, reproducing, extending, and creating patterns using
manipulatives, sounds, and actions. [C, CN, PS, V]

40CED81D274648C48C9288AAE5DE2268.description: Count the number of objects in a given set, rearrange the objects, predict the new count, and recount to verify the prediction.

F447512233FB488C87AB87C3A547185A.description: In a fixed arrangement, starting in different locations, show that the count of the number of objects in a set does not change.

58A8FC5FAABE47D9828922E0FAFCC41F.description: Answer the question, How many are in the set? using the last number counted in a set.

245D45CBB5824ED78C98052751A400FF.description: Students will be expected to demonstrate an understanding of counting to 10. [C, CN, ME, PS, R, V]

7717000474B2420997DEA10D29769459.description: Compare two given sets through direct comparison and describe the sets using words such as more, fewer, as many as, or the same number as.

CD3BB75035D84E20A6E5B0768A0E0EF3.description: Construct a set to show more than, fewer than, or as many as a given set.

3F5CB8BAAF1E4DCDBED9A2746A6C28EC.description:
Students will be expected to compare sets containing 1 to 10 objects, using one-to-one
correspondence.
[C, CN, V]

5A6C2C3D95874DFE8353579D9D381A5F.description: Show a given number as two parts, using pictures, and name the number of objects in each part.

EBF4164A7FB64930819C8D7D9C48C90B.description: Show a given number as two parts (using fingers, counters, or other objects) and name the number of objects in each part.

987EE1B1941D4D2383DC6C379EE7FA13.description:
